title: The One With Rachels Going Away Party

jokes.text: Heads, I win. Tails, you lose.
jokes.setup: Joey proposes a coin toss to stop Rachel from moving to Paris, with apparent stakes on both sides.
jokes.punchline: Joey reveals the coin toss is rigged — both outcomes favor him — but he still manages to lose 57 times in a row.
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey naivety — he tries to cheat at a coin toss with the oldest trick in the book, yet still manages to lose repeatedly. The character integration is excellent; only Joey would attempt this and fail so spectacularly. The punchline lands because we realize the magnitude of his incompetence retroactively at 07:43.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, so heads I win, tails you lose.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, that's the same thing!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I know.

jokes.text: Tails! / Damn it!
jokes.setup: Joey has just explained that heads he wins and tails she loses — a rigged toss.
jokes.punchline: The coin lands tails and Rachel wins anyway, exposing Joey's failed scheme instantly.
jokes.explanation: The immediate payoff of the rigged-coin setup. Economy is excellent — two words ('Damn it!') convey the punchline perfectly. Works as a quick button on the opening joke.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, heads I win, tails you lose.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: That's the same thing!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No it's not. If it's heads, I win. If it's tails, you lose.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Joey, those are the same outcome!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, okay, fine. Heads I win, tails... it doesn't count.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: How does tails not count?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: We flip again.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You'll flip it a thousand times!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm a very patient man.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Fine. Flip.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay... tails.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: That's tails. You have to flip again.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, okay... tails again.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Again.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: This is crazy! How is this happening?!

jokes.text: Hey, Rach, you're leaving tomorrow. Shouldn't you be packing? / It's all done.
jokes.setup: Chandler assumes Rachel, notorious for being high-maintenance and disorganized, hasn't packed.
jokes.punchline: Rachel reveals everything is meticulously sorted — luggage, shipping boxes, even the plane sandwich.
jokes.explanation: Mild character reversal — Rachel being hyper-organized subverts expectations built over 10 seasons. Competent but not special.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: See? I'm completely packed and organized.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Look at me, I'm so casual now. I just threw a towel on the floor.

jokes.text: And after I took a shower this morning, I just threw my towel on the floor. / Oh, God, it hurts to even joke about it.
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are reflecting on Rachel's departure; Monica mentions she threw her towel on the floor as a joke.
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately breaks character — the idea of doing that genuinely pains her, exposing her compulsive neatness.
jokes.explanation: Strong character integration — this is 100% Monica. The joke is in her inability to even pretend to be messy. The self-awareness makes it sharper than a simple Monica-is-neat gag.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm just gonna throw this towel on the floor.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Who cares? It's just a towel.

jokes.text: Oh, my God. I have nothing left to teach you.
jokes.setup: Rachel shows Monica her perfectly organized travel documents arranged in the order she'll need them.
jokes.punchline: Monica, the obsessive organizer, is moved to awe — implying she is the master who trained Rachel in the art of organization.
jokes.explanation: Good economy — the sensei-student framing is implicit but lands clearly. Monica treating document organization like a martial art is good character work.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I made a sandwich for the plane. I mean, you never know what they're going to serve, and I wanted to be prepared.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Rachel, it's a transatlantic flight. They serve meals.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, what if I don't like it? What if it's weird European food?

jokes.text: At what point did it stop being funny that I took her passport?
jokes.setup: Ross secretly took Rachel's passport, sending her into a panic, and watches her desperately search through boxes.
jokes.punchline: Ross's talking-head confession reveals his prank extended way past the comedically appropriate moment — his deadpan self-awareness punctures the joke.
jokes.explanation: Smart joke with genuine meta-awareness. Ross asking himself when the prank stopped being funny is a good bit of self-examination that also characterizes him as simultaneously mischievous and neurotic. The extended pause before the talking-head (from 01:27 to 02:24) adds to the comedy — we're left with Rachel frantically searching while Ross presumably watches for a full minute. Good structural use of the confessional format.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Look at you! You've organized the entire closet by color and fabric weight!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, I learned from the best.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm so proud. You've finally embraced your inner control freak. It's beautiful. I think I'm gonna cry.

jokes.text: ...but your hand's kind of blocking the part where the baby's gonna come out.
jokes.setup: Monica asks Erica if she minds Monica touching her pregnant belly.
jokes.punchline: Erica matter-of-factly tells Monica she's touching the birth canal area, stated with zero embarrassment.
jokes.explanation: Good deadpan from Erica — the frank anatomical specificity creates the cringe. Works because it's delivered without embarrassment, making Monica (and the audience) more uncomfortable than Erica.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Joey, where is my passport?! We leave in three hours!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Your passport? It's... it's in my pocket.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: WHAT?! How long have you had it?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Since this morning. I was gonna give it back, but then you started freaking out and it got funny, and then it got less funny, and now it's just... really not funny.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: It was NEVER funny, Joey!

jokes.text: I'm just always afraid that people think I'm just fat with big breasts.
jokes.setup: Chandler awkwardly stares at Erica's chest after she arrives visibly pregnant.
jokes.punchline: Erica voices her genuine fear about how people perceive her body during pregnancy — which inadvertently draws more attention to exactly what Chandler was staring at.
jokes.explanation: The situational irony is solid — she raises the concern while Chandler is literally doing what she describes. Decent but not outstanding.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: That's not the baby.

jokes.text: Okay, well, stop staring at them. / She brought them up.
jokes.setup: Monica catches Chandler staring at Erica's breasts after Erica mentions them.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's defense — 'She brought them up' — is both literally and figuratively true, and completely fails as a defense.
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler awkward-deflection joke. The wordplay ('brought them up') is subtle but adds a layer. His terrible defense is perfect character comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: Well, I'm pregnant.

jokes.text: Erica, those things aren't free. In fact, they have one of the highest markups of any consumer product-- / Ross, she's giving us her baby. She can eat you if she wants.
jokes.setup: Erica mentions the hotel minibar snacks are free; Ross begins a pedantic lecture about minibar pricing.
jokes.punchline: Monica cuts him off with a savage, absurdist threat — Erica can literally eat Ross if she wants because of the gift she's giving them.
jokes.explanation: Monica's line is the standout — the hyperbolic 'she can eat you' is delightfully absurd while also being emotionally grounded (they owe Erica everything). Ross's nerdy pedantry sets it up perfectly. Good economy and strong character work for both.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: I know I'm huge. I feel like a water buffalo.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You're not huge, you're pregnant.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, tell that to the guy at the grocery store who asked me when I was due. I told him nine months. He said, 'All of them?'

jokes.text: No, no. This will always be your place. It would be too sad. / Plus, how much a month does it cost to feed Joey?
jokes.setup: Chandler declines taking over Monica's apartment with a sentimental reason.
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately adds the real, practical reason — feeding Joey is prohibitively expensive.
jokes.explanation: Good deflation joke — Chandler's sweet sentiment is immediately undercut by Monica's practical concern about Joey's food budget. Works as running commentary on Joey's appetite, a long-established character trait.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: What? Why are you staring at my breasts?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I wasn't staring! I was just... looking to see if you had a... pen in your pocket.

jokes.text: Hmm. Packing. Sexy cheerleader comedy. / Hmm. Helpful brother. Creepy loner at teen movie. / Creepy!
jokes.setup: Ross is asked to help Chandler and Joey pack instead of going to see a movie.
jokes.punchline: Ross internally deliberates between helping his brother-in-law pack and going to a 'sexy cheerleader comedy' alone — then immediately categorizes himself as the 'creepy loner' and chooses to help.
jokes.explanation: Ross's self-aware categorization of himself as 'creepy loner' is good character comedy. The deliberation format and the swift self-condemnation lands. Slightly bloated with the three-line structure.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, you guys, this place is amazing! And look at this minibar – everything's free!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Erica, no, honey, you have to pay for those.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: What? But it's right there in the room!

jokes.text: Try it. I can't feel a thing. / Are you kidding? / This is packing? / We're taking a break. / From? / Jumping on the bed.
jokes.setup: Ross enters to find Chandler and Joey apparently doing something with Styrofoam packing material.
jokes.punchline: They reveal they've been jumping on the bed with Styrofoam — a completely childish activity dressed up as a 'break' from packing.
jokes.explanation: Solid visual gag with good escalation — the reveal that they're on break from something they haven't even started is classic Joey/Chandler regression humor. The physical comedy of them jumping on the bed would amplify this significantly on screen.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: These items in the minibar are free, right?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, no, they're not free. The hotel charges you for everything you take out of the minibar. It's actually a significant markup—usually 300 to 400 percent above retail value. So when you see a candy bar that normally costs 75 cents, they're charging you three dollars. It's one of the ways hotels generate revenue from their guests.

jokes.text: Let's put Styrofoam peanuts down his pants and kick him!
jokes.setup: Ross takes charge as the responsible adult, telling the guys to get serious about packing.
jokes.punchline: Ross immediately suggests a completely juvenile prank — undercutting his own authority in the most unexpected way.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The setup is a perfect fake-out — Ross steps into the responsible role, echoes Monica, and then immediately blows it with an absurdly specific and violent suggestion. 'Let's put Styrofoam peanuts DOWN HIS PANTS and KICK HIM' is both unexpected and oddly specific in a way that makes it funnier. The specificity of 'down his pants' and the kicking elevates it from a generic subversion to something genuinely quotable. Strong economy and structure.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: We have to keep her happy! If Erica is not happy, she could change her mind and keep the babies!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Monica, she's not going to change her mind.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You don't know that! We have to do everything she wants. If she wanted me to chop off my arm, I would chop off my arm!

jokes.text: Joey, you pack them, and Ross, you repack whatever Joey packs.
jokes.setup: Chandler organizes the packing workflow.
jokes.punchline: He builds in a correction step specifically for Joey's inevitably wrong packing — treating it as a known system flaw.
jokes.explanation: Economical character joke — Chandler's managerial instinct to build a correction protocol around Joey's incompetence is both funny and efficient. The joke works in one line.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Joey, if you move in, you'd have to pay rent.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: How much?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Half of what Chandler pays.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That's perfect! I can just eat half as much food.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, that's not how rent works.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, it should be!

jokes.text: You guys hear a ringing?
jokes.setup: Chandler has just delivered the logical system for packing that implicitly insults Joey.
jokes.punchline: Joey's response is to hear a phantom ringing — implying either he didn't process the insult or is blissfully changing the subject. The ringing turns out to be handcuffs.
jokes.explanation: Joey's obliviousness is well-deployed here — it's also a transitional beat to the handcuffs discovery. Functions more as a bridge joke than a standalone.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, okay, I know I should help you pack, but The Matrix is playing and I've already seen it three times, so really, I'm not missing anything new. Plus, the statistical probability of me actually enjoying a fourth viewing is inversely proportional to the diminishing returns on—

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Ross, just go to the movie.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? I'm being analytical about my leisure time preferences!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, you're being annoying about your leisure time preferences.

jokes.text: Hey, handcuffs. And fur-lined. Nice. / I didn't know you guys had it in you.
jokes.setup: Joey finds fur-lined handcuffs in the guest room closet while packing.
jokes.punchline: Chandler and Joey immediately assume they belong to Monica and Chandler, impressed by an apparently kinky side they didn't know about.
jokes.explanation: Initiates the handcuffs running gag that pays off multiple times through the episode. 'I didn't know you guys had it in you' is delivered with Joey's characteristic sincerity making it land well. Rewatch bonus because it sets up a chain of callbacks.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What are you guys doing? We have to pack!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I know, I know. But look at this — I've numbed my entire hand. I can't feel anything.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: See? Nothing. It's like it's not even there.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler, that's your foot.

jokes.text: Chandler, you don't have a sister, so you can't understand how much this bums me out. / I didn't know Monica had these. / Maybe she used them with another boyfriend. Maybe Richard.
jokes.setup: Ross is upset thinking the handcuffs belong to Monica and might connect to her past.
jokes.punchline: Chandler/Ross speculates Monica used them with Richard — a sore subject — inserting the Monica's ex-boyfriend rivalry in an absurd context.
jokes.explanation: Ross's brotherly anxiety combined with Chandler's insecurity about Richard is good character layering. The Richard mention is reliable crowd-pleaser territory.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: How's the packing going?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Great!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, we're making really good time.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What are you doing right now?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: We're taking a break.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: We were jumping on the bed.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Jumping on the bed?! We're moving!

jokes.text: Why would she use them with Richard and not me? I can be kinky. / I once did a naked dance for her with scarves.
jokes.setup: Chandler reacts to the possibility Monica used handcuffs with Richard but not him.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's defense of his kinkiness is a 'naked scarf dance' — an image so awkward and specific that it becomes funnier the more you visualize it.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. 'Naked scarf dance' is an absurdly specific image that is hilarious because it's both trying to be sexy and inherently ridiculous. The escalation from 'I can be kinky' to this particular act is perfect Chandler — his awkwardness expressed through a genuinely baffling attempt at romance. High originality, excellent character integration (this is quintessentially Chandler), and very quotable. The specificity of 'with scarves' does enormous comedic work.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, we need to get serious about packing.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No more fooling around, no more jokes. This is it.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: We pack now, we're done by tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So... who wants to help me wrap Chandler's entire apartment in plastic wrap?

jokes.text: Bumming hard, guys. Bumming hard.
jokes.setup: Chandler has just shared the naked scarf dance anecdote while Ross is trying to be emotionally present about Monica's supposed kink life.
jokes.punchline: Ross's deadpan 'bumming hard' captures the exact combination of too-much-information discomfort and brotherly exasperation.
jokes.explanation: Extremely economical reaction beat. 'Bumming hard, guys. Bumming hard.' is a perfect button — the repetition adds emphasis without bloat. Ross's brotherly discomfort is well-deployed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, Joey, you're in charge of packing the kitchen stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Got it!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, wait, I'm coming with you.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Why? Don't you trust me?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: It's not about trust. It's about the fact that last time you packed, you put a casserole dish in a box labeled 'FRAGILE' upside down, next to a carton of eggs.

jokes.text: It's kind of like being married to a rock star, you know? My husband has a gig. / Yeah? Where is it? / Oh, he's playing organ for a children's roller-skating party.
jokes.setup: Phoebe romanticizes Mike's absence by calling him a 'rock star' with a 'gig.'
jokes.punchline: The gig is playing organ at a children's roller-skating party — the most un-rock-star venue imaginable.
jokes.explanation: Excellent misdirection with clean structure. 'Rock star' expectation is fully subverted by 'children's roller-skating party' and the specific instrument choice of 'organ' makes it even funnier. Phoebe's sunny obliviousness to the gap between her framing and reality is perfect character work.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh my God! Chandler, you dog! Where did you get these?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Those aren't mine!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, right. And I'm not Joey Tribbiani.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: They're Monica's!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Even better!

jokes.text: Rock on!
jokes.setup: Phoebe has just revealed Mike's very unglamorous gig.
jokes.punchline: Monica's flat 'Rock on!' acknowledges the irony without belaboring it.
jokes.explanation: Functional button on the previous joke. Works primarily because of its brevity and timing, not its originality.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! Handcuffs?!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Those are... those are mine. From work.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I did NOT need to know that my sister and my best friend—

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Ugh! Why would you even—I can't unsee this!

jokes.text: Smoked oyster casserole with a breakfast-cereal crust. / Kidney beans in their own juices, and for dessert, a questionable orange.
jokes.setup: Monica has prepared food for the party using items she doesn't want to move to the new house.
jokes.punchline: The menu is progressively more disgusting and absurd — culminating in 'a questionable orange' as a dessert course.
jokes.explanation: Genuinely funny list joke with strong escalation. Monica, the great chef, serving 'kidney beans in their own juices' subverts her entire character. 'A questionable orange' as a dessert is an inspired punchline — the word 'questionable' does heavy lifting. Good originality.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, hey, hey! Maybe it was her ex-boyfriend!

jokes.text: What did I just say? (after everyone says 'Hey Rach' and she cries)
jokes.setup: Chandler explicitly warns everyone not to say anything emotional to Rachel, then the whole group immediately greets her warmly, making her cry.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's exasperated 'What did I just say?' as everyone ignores his warning.
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom beat but executed well. The setup-immediate-reversal structure is tight and Chandler's exasperation is a good character note.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, maybe I like handcuffs! Maybe I have a whole drawer full of them! Maybe I'm into some pretty interesting stuff!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You don't know what goes on behind closed doors!

jokes.text: It feels like when Melrose Place got canceled.
jokes.setup: Joey is emotionally processing that Rachel is leaving — comparing it to losing a person he loves.
jokes.punchline: He equates Rachel's departure with a TV show cancellation, then doubles down: 'Ah, forget it, I miss Melrose Place.'
jokes.explanation: Perfect Joey characterization — his emotional hierarchy places a TV show on par with a close friend. The beat where he catches himself and then says 'Ah forget it, I miss Melrose Place' is a great self-correction that reveals he still can't prioritize correctly. High character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I can be kinky.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Last week I wore my socks to bed.

jokes.text: Who loses 57 coin tosses in a row? You know? / Heads, she wins. Tails, I lose.
jokes.setup: Joey reflects on his failed attempts to stop Rachel from leaving via coin toss.
jokes.punchline: Joey finally realizes the coin toss was rigged — against him — but it took him 57 losses to notice.
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The callback reveals that Rachel had been running the same trick on Joey — and he STILL didn't figure it out until 57 losses in. The escalation from the opening (we knew Joey was trying to cheat) to this reveal (Joey was being cheated the whole time, 57 times!) is structurally brilliant. 'Who loses 57 coin tosses in a row?' is the perfect setup for his dawning realization. High marks across the board — it's funny, character-specific (only Joey), and pays off a cold-open joke in a deeply satisfying way. Joey correcting himself to 'Heads, she wins. Tails, I lose' in real time is the perfect button.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I could have gone my whole life without knowing that.

jokes.text: Wait a minute. / Yes, Joe? / I forgot to pick up my dry cleaning.
jokes.setup: Joey dramatically says 'Wait a minute' — implying he's had a major revelation about the coin toss.
jokes.punchline: He's actually remembered he forgot his dry cleaning.
jokes.explanation: Good misdirection — the dramatic 'Wait a minute' primes us for a revelation, but Joey's mind has already moved on entirely to mundane concerns. Works as a quick button on the coin toss sequence.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Mike's actually playing a huge gig tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, he's really made it big. He's performing for thousands of people.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: They're all screaming his name, totally into it.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: He's at the Riverside skating rink playing organ for a kids' birthday party.

jokes.text: In six months, the statute of limitations runs out and I can travel internationally again.
jokes.setup: Rachel asks friends if they'll come visit her in Paris.
jokes.punchline: Chandler casually reveals he can't currently travel internationally — implying he has some unspecified legal trouble abroad — without any further explanation.
jokes.explanation: Funny throwaway that implies a whole backstory with zero exposition. The specificity of 'six months' and 'statute of limitations' makes it funnier than a vague 'I can't travel.' Classic Chandler background absurdity — he has some international legal problem and treats it as completely casual conversation.

dialogue.speaker: Mike
dialogue.line: Yeah, nothing says 'rock and roll' like playing organ at a children's roller skating party.

jokes.text: If I had to guess, I'd say Rachel's putting on the bubble wrap, and Phoebe's doing the punching.
jokes.setup: Joey wonders what Rachel and Phoebe are doing in the other room for so long.
jokes.punchline: Chandler speculates they're doing a bubble-wrap sensory activity — with Phoebe doing the punching — a perfectly plausible activity for Phoebe.
jokes.explanation: Good character observation — 'Phoebe's doing the punching' is the kind of Phoebe-specific detail that rings true and gets a laugh. The specificity elevates what could be a generic joke.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I made a casserole with whatever was left in the fridge. It's a disgusting combination of leftover ingredients.

jokes.text: If I had to guess, I'd say... Rachel's putting on the bubble wrap, and Phoebe's doing the punching.
jokes.setup: Rachel has taken Phoebe aside for a private goodbye. The others wonder what's going on in the other room.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's theory of their activity is that Rachel is wearing bubble wrap and Phoebe is punching her — an absurd but somehow plausible Phoebe-specific activity.
jokes.explanation: A good joke that derives its humor from Chandler's characterization of Phoebe as someone for whom bubble-wrap punching is a plausible goodbye ritual. The specificity (Rachel in bubble wrap, Phoebe punching) makes it land. Character comedy that could only be about Phoebe.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, so I have some leftover Chinese food from Tuesday, a casserole that's been here since last month, some mystery meat in a container I'm afraid to open, and...a questionable orange.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: A questionable orange? Monica, it's either orange or it's not orange.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well that's the problem—I'm not sure anymore.

jokes.text: It's a cotton swab with a bit of my saliva on it so that if they perfect the cloning process while you're over there, you can use the DNA to create your own Pheebs.
jokes.setup: Phoebe gives Rachel a going-away gift — a cotton swab.
jokes.punchline: The cotton swab is Phoebe's saliva — for cloning purposes — in case the technology advances while Rachel is in Paris.
jokes.explanation: Quintessential Phoebe joke — absurdist premise delivered with complete sincerity and logic. 'Your own Pheebs' as a gift concept is both hilarious and touching in its way. The idea that Phoebe's greatest going-away gift is the possibility of cloning herself is perfect character integration. High originality because the premise is genuinely unusual.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I can't believe Rachel's leaving. This is like when they cancelled my favorite show.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, Rachel leaving is a little more serious than a TV show getting cancelled.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, no. You don't understand. I was really invested in that show.

jokes.text: I'm gonna throw this away... but thank you so much for the gesture.
jokes.setup: Phoebe has given Rachel a saliva-covered cotton swab as a going-away gift.
jokes.punchline: Rachel immediately announces she's throwing it away while still thanking Phoebe for the thought.
jokes.explanation: Perfect straight-man button. Rachel's immediate 'I'm gonna throw this away' is funny because she doesn't even pretend to value it, but 'the gesture' saves the interaction from being cruel. Good economy — the pause before 'but thank you' is the joke.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: It's like Melrose Place, you know? All the drama, all the relationships...

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Who am I kidding? I just really miss that show, man.

jokes.text: Oh, yes, I decided to leave those out for you in case Richard stops by and you want to engage in a little light bondage and mustache play.
jokes.setup: Chandler finds the fur-lined handcuffs on his pillow and confronts Monica.
jokes.punchline: Monica sarcastically claims she left the handcuffs out for Chandler to use with Richard — weaponizing his insecurity about her ex.
jokes.explanation: 'Mustache play' is a great coinage — specific enough to be funny on its own. Monica weaponizing the Richard insecurity is good marital banter. The phrase 'light bondage and mustache play' has genuine quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I've tried everything to stop Rachel from winning at coin tosses.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, she's been flipping the coin with her thumb the whole time.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, what? That's cheating!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: It's not cheating if you don't know about it.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: How did I not notice that?

jokes.text: Good luck getting another scarf dance from me.
jokes.setup: Monica challenges Chandler's claim that the handcuffs aren't hers, implying she's being blamed.
jokes.punchline: Chandler threatens to withhold his naked scarf dance — his self-described kinky move — as punishment.
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback — the idea that Chandler threatening to withhold the scarf dance is a punishment (when it's clearly not) makes it funnier. Monica's reaction ('That would be a terrible punishment') is the perfect button.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, so here's the thing about the rules. Rule number one: you gotta let her know you're interested, but you gotta do it casually.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Rule number two: you establish yourself as a friend first. No, wait—you establish yourself as a potential romantic interest while still being a friend.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Rule number three: you never, ever appear too eager. But you also can't appear too uninterested.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: And rule number four: you gotta play it cool, but not so cool that she thinks you're not interested.

jokes.text: That would be a terrible punishment.
jokes.setup: Chandler threatens to withhold his naked scarf dance.
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately and dryly confirms that losing the scarf dance would be absolutely no loss at all.
jokes.explanation: Perfect button — five words that maximize the callback. Monica's deadpan delivery would make this hit harder on screen.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait a minute... all those coin tosses... they were all heads!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh my God, that's amazing! Do you know what this means?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I need to pick up my dry cleaning before 6!

jokes.text: Rachel. With handcuffs. / Interesting. / Joey's bare ass. / Well played.
jokes.setup: Chandler floats the idea that the handcuffs might be Rachel's, based on her history in the guest room.
jokes.punchline: Everyone collectively imagines Rachel with handcuffs, then Ross immediately brings up 'Joey's bare ass' as the competing mental image — and Monica declares it 'well played.'
jokes.explanation: Good escalating beat — the rapid-fire 'Rachel. With handcuffs.' pause followed by 'Joey's bare ass' as a competing thought is well-structured. 'Well played' as Monica's acknowledgment is a nice meta-comedic touch. The economy of the exchange (four short phrases) is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You guys are gonna come visit me in Paris, right?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, I would love to, but I can't leave the country.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Why not?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm not supposed to leave the country.

jokes.text: Well played. [Chandler's reaction to learning Joey's bare ass is somehow involved]
jokes.setup: Monica reveals Joey's bare ass is implicated in the handcuff mystery.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's admiringly deadpan 'Well played' — as if complimenting a chess move — applied to whatever kinky situation involved both handcuffs and Joey.
jokes.explanation: A quick button on the Joey reveal. 'Well played' in this context is funny for its gentlemanly approval of an apparently scandalous situation. Economy is its best quality.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I wonder what Rachel and Phoebe do when they say goodbye to each other.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh, they do this whole thing. They lock eyes, take each other's hands, and silently communicate their feelings for about forty-five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Really?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No! But wouldn't that be weird?

jokes.text: Please... Please don't-- Don't turn into, you know, a French bitch.
jokes.setup: Phoebe and Rachel are having a tearful, heartfelt goodbye.
jokes.punchline: In the middle of her emotional plea, Phoebe's deepest fear is that Rachel will become a 'French bitch' — delivered with complete earnestness.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. The tonal pivot from tearful sincerity to 'French bitch' is perfectly timed. The halting delivery — 'Please don't... Don't turn into, you know, a French bitch' — with 'you know' bridging the gap is excellent writing. It's funny, quotable, and characterizes Phoebe perfectly: she's loving and protective but expresses it in the most unexpected way. High marks across craft dimensions.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I got you a gift. It's a hair sample kit. So when you're older and you want to clone yourself, you'll have the DNA.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, that's... that's very thoughtful.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I know! And I kept one for myself. So we can be clones together!

jokes.text: Are you wearing waterproof mascara? / No. / Oh, you're so screwed.
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are about to have their emotional goodbye.
jokes.punchline: Monica's practical concern about mascara before crying is immediately followed by horror at Rachel's answer.
jokes.explanation: Clean three-line joke with good economy. Monica's concern for Rachel's cosmetics in the midst of raw emotion is a perfect character note — she can't help being practical. 'You're so screwed' as the punch is well-timed.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Phoebe, that is so sweet, but I have to be honest with you—I'm gonna throw this away the second you leave.

jokes.text: Now I know how my students feel at the end of each year. / And why they act out by giving me such bad evaluations.
jokes.setup: Ross says he understands the sadness of parting, comparing himself to a teacher saying goodbye to students.
jokes.punchline: He then reveals the students give him terrible evaluations — undercutting his self-flattering teacher-student analogy.
jokes.explanation: Good self-own joke for Ross. He sets up a flattering comparison and then accidentally reveals the students hate him and express it through bad evaluations. The two-beat structure works well and 'act out by giving me such bad evaluations' is specific and funny.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Maybe it's from one of your exes. You know, as a parting gift. Like a going away present, but for your wrists.

jokes.text: What? / See you every day! (Both Monica and Rachel crying and barely comprehensible)
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel's goodbye speech becomes increasingly tearful until they can no longer speak coherently.
jokes.punchline: Their emotional conversation devolves into incomprehensible sobbing — the audience can hear only fragments of their heartfelt words.
jokes.explanation: More of an emotional moment than a pure comedy beat, but the incomprehensibility of their crying is played for laughs. The audience recognition of this experience makes it land, but it's broad rather than crafted comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Fine. Fine! But I'm taking back my awkward kinky dance.

jokes.text: Oh, no, she took down Monica. / And I'm the crier in the family.
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel's goodbye has dissolved into full crying; the guys watch from across the room.
jokes.punchline: Ross's horror that Monica has been emotionally 'taken down,' and his self-identification as the family's designated crier.
jokes.explanation: Solid character beat — Ross's possessive relationship with crying ('I'm the crier in the family') is a funny claim. The sports-commentary framing of Monica being 'taken down' is good.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: If you don't stop criticizing me, I'm going to stop doing the scarf dance.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh no, not the scarf dance. How will I go on?

jokes.text: Maybe she won't talk to me if it looks like we're in conversation. / Okay. / That thing you said about the thing... it really made me think about that other thing. / Rach? / Oh, it's okay, Chandler's talking to her.
jokes.setup: Ross is desperate to avoid being emotionally confronted by Rachel's goodbye.
jokes.punchline: He and Joey fake a conversation using entirely meaningless filler dialogue ('that thing... that other thing') to ward Rachel off. It works — Chandler intercepts instead.
jokes.explanation: Good physical comedy implied in the dialogue — Ross and Joey visibly pantomiming deep conversation. The placeholder dialogue ('that thing... that other thing') is funny in its specificity of being nonspecific.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. These are Rachel's handcuffs?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Tell me everything.

jokes.text: Oh, I'm sure gonna miss pretending to laugh at your weird jokes that I don't get.
jokes.setup: Chandler and Rachel are having a moment before she realizes he's holding the handcuffs.
jokes.punchline: Chandler pre-emptively deflects with a self-deprecating joke about his own humor, implying Rachel has always fake-laughed at him.
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler self-deprecation — he exposes his own emotional defense mechanism while still being funny. The implication that Rachel has been politely fake-laughing for 10 years is a nice long-game joke.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wait, Rachel's into what?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, just shut up about it.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, no, tell me more!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Fine. Joey!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Drop your pants.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What the—

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: There. Satisfied? Can we please never speak of this again?

jokes.text: Oh, I'm sure gonna miss pretending to laugh at your weird jokes that I don't get.
jokes.setup: Chandler finds himself handing Rachel's handcuffs back to her and uses the moment to begin his own goodbye.
jokes.punchline: His goodbye line is simultaneously affectionate and brutally honest: he's been fake-laughing at her jokes for years without understanding them, and he will MISS doing that.
jokes.explanation: A sweet and funny goodbye line. The honesty of 'pretending to laugh at your weird jokes' is both funny and oddly touching — it's a strange thing to miss but a very real, specific detail of friendship. Character-appropriate for Chandler's mix of awkward sincerity and self-deprecating humor.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wow, that's a good tactic. I'm not even mad.

jokes.text: I think you're forgetting the kinkiest former resident of that room. / Pheebs! / Yeah!
jokes.setup: Everyone is trying to figure out whose handcuffs they are, running through Monica, Rachel...
jokes.punchline: Chandler points to Phoebe as the kinkiest former resident — Phoebe enthusiastically agrees.
jokes.explanation: Excellent use of Phoebe's character — her enthusiastic 'Yeah!' confirming that she is indeed the kinkiest is perfect. The reveal lands well as a misdirection payoff and Phoebe's self-confirmation is the ideal button.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm gonna miss you so much. But I'm worried that if you stay in Paris, you're gonna become all French and you won't want to be my friend anymore.

jokes.text: These are not mine. Look how flimsy they are. Come on. / My God, you try to hang a guy from a water pipe with these, they'll snap like a piece of licorice.
jokes.setup: Chandler presents the handcuffs to Phoebe as likely hers; she denies ownership.
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's denial is based not on the concept but on quality — she considers them substandard for the specific purpose of hanging a man from a water pipe.
jokes.explanation: The best joke in the episode by a significant margin. The genius is in what Phoebe DOESN'T deny — she doesn't say 'I don't do that,' she says these particular handcuffs are too FLIMSY for hanging a man from a water pipe. The comparison to licorice ('they'll snap like a piece of licorice') is inspired — it's specific, absurd, and domestic. This is 100% Phoebe — only she would evaluate bondage equipment by tensile strength needed for pipe suspension. Comparable in quality to the vasectomy anchor example in its escalation and character specificity. High marks across all craft dimensions.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Why are you wearing so much makeup?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What do you mean? I always wear this much.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Not on a day like today. You're going to cry it all off anyway.

jokes.text: Where do you think Mike really is?
jokes.setup: Chandler asks Phoebe about her claimed water-pipe hanging activities.
jokes.punchline: Chandler implies Mike (at his 'gig') might actually be handcuffed to a water pipe by Phoebe — recontextualizing the earlier roller-skating party joke.
jokes.explanation: Excellent economy — five words that do enormous work. The callback connects Mike's 'gig' (which we already found suspicious/funny) with Phoebe's water-pipe hanging habit, implying Mike is literally tied up somewhere. The implication without explanation is perfect dark comedy. This is the best callback in the episode after the coin toss reveal.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I know how you feel. Saying goodbye is one of the hardest things to do.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I had to say goodbye to my students at the university, and it was devastating.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Although, to be fair, based on my teaching reviews, they seemed pretty happy to say goodbye to me.

jokes.text: [Chandler and Rachel hugging — fart noise] / I'm sorry, give me one more chance. / [Second fart noise] / Oh! / I'm sorry. Just go. Just go. / I can't. I can't.
jokes.setup: After Chandler's heartfelt emotional goodbye, they hug.
jokes.punchline: The hug produces a fart noise (from the leather couch or similar), destroying the moment. Chandler tries again, same result. Both dissolve into laughter.
jokes.explanation: Broad physical comedy that works in context — the tonal whiplash from genuine emotion to fart noise is classic multi-cam execution. The second attempt making it worse is good escalation. Not sophisticated comedy but very effective for a broad audience and emotionally welcome relief.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm going to be fine. I'm going to be strong.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, oh my God, oh my God! I can't believe you're leaving! Who's going to help me pick out curtains? Who's going to listen to me complain about my job? Who's going to...

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't do this! I can't say goodbye!

jokes.text: [Hug fart sound effect] — Chandler's goodbye hug with Rachel produces an accidental fart sound.
jokes.setup: Chandler and Rachel have just shared a genuinely emotional goodbye. They go in for a hug.
jokes.punchline: The hug produces what sounds like a fart (from clothing/air compression). The emotional moment is completely deflated by the bodily function sound.
jokes.explanation: The hug fart is a crowd-pleaser that works through perfect timing — it punctures a genuine emotional moment with a universally relatable embarrassment. It's not sophisticated comedy, but its placement (immediately after an earnest goodbye speech) gives it impact beyond its craft. The 'cheap' score is appropriately lower — this is pure physical comedy without wit, but it's well-executed.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh no, if Monica's crying, I'm doomed.

jokes.text: You cried yesterday at the 6:00 news. / That old woman was being scammed by her mechanic.
jokes.setup: Chandler acknowledges he hasn't cried like that in years; Ross calls him on it.
jokes.punchline: Ross reveals he cried at a news segment about a mechanic scam — and defends it as completely reasonable.
jokes.explanation: Good deflation joke — Ross's earnest defense of crying at the mechanic story is perfect character comedy. The specificity ('the 6:00 news,' 'mechanic') elevates it above a generic 'Ross cried' joke.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So, uh... how about that... local sports team?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, they really... did stuff this season.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Mm-hmm, and the way they... played the game.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Definitely played it.

jokes.text: What? / I don't get a goodbye? / Lucky bastard.
jokes.setup: Rachel leaves the party after saying goodbye to everyone — except Ross — and Joey reacts.
jokes.punchline: Joey's 'Lucky bastard' about Ross — implying being skipped by Rachel's tearful goodbye is a blessing.
jokes.explanation: Good economy and sharp reaction beat. Joey's perspective — that avoiding an emotionally devastating goodbye is lucky — reframes Ross's hurt in a funny way.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So... how about that weather?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I know, right? It's been crazy. Was it raining when you came in?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, a little.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: See, I told you! I was like, 'It's gonna rain today.' And then it did!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wow.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah! And you know what else? I think it might rain tomorrow too.

jokes.text: Well, maybe she thought that with all of your history, it could be, you know, implicit. / Well, it needs to be 'plicit.'
jokes.setup: Chandler suggests Rachel's omission of Ross might mean the goodbye was 'implicit' given their history.
jokes.punchline: Ross demands it be 'plicit' — shortening 'explicit' by dropping the 'ex' — which is both a wordplay gag and an emotional outburst.
jokes.explanation: Clever wordplay that works on two levels: it's a good pun (implicit vs. 'plicit'/explicit) and it characterizes Ross's emotional state — he's so flustered he's mangling language. The word-fragment gag is sharp and quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Goodbye, Chandler. I have to tell you... I've been faking laughs at your jokes this whole time.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? All of them?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Pretty much, yeah.

jokes.text: I mean, don't I deserve anything? A few tears, a cursory hug? / Not from you!
jokes.setup: Ross laments not getting a goodbye from Rachel.
jokes.punchline: Chandler aggressively agrees that Ross specifically does not deserve a goodbye — then immediately realizes what he said.
jokes.explanation: Good quick moment — Chandler's emphatic 'Not from you!' before catching himself is a funny accidental honesty beat. Brief but effective.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Whose handcuffs are these?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Those aren't mine.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, they have to be somebody's. Phoebe, come on, you're the kinky one.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm not kinky!

jokes.text: And say what? You owe me a goodbye? / I mean, he's got more pride than that. / The hell I do!
jokes.setup: Chandler suggests Ross should go confront Rachel; Ross resists with dignity.
jokes.punchline: Ross immediately abandons his stated pride and storms off.
jokes.explanation: 'The hell I do!' is a great instant capitulation — Ross's self-awareness of his own lack of pride is very good character work. The structure (pride claim → immediate denial) is tight.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, they're not very good handcuffs. The left one digs into your wrist, and the chain is too short. Plus, there's this weird smell...

jokes.text: Huh? Be best friends with you? Go out with you? Have a baby with you? Oh, wait a minute. Wait a minute! I did all those things!
jokes.setup: Ross storms to Rachel's door demanding a goodbye. He asks rhetorically what he has to do to earn one.
jokes.punchline: Ross lists hypothetical things one would need to do to deserve a goodbye — 'be best friends with you, go out with you, have a baby with you' — and then stops cold as he realizes he has done ALL of them.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's strongest jokes and arguably the best character moment for Ross in the episode. The escalating list of 'hypotheticals' building toward the self-aware realization is perfectly constructed — the audience sees the punchline coming half a beat before Ross does, which creates the comedic tension. 'Wait a minute. Wait a minute! I DID all those things!' with the dawning horror is Ross at his best: ridiculous, self-pitying, but somehow completely justified. Easily an 8+ moment.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: How do you know so much about handcuffs?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, I have my ways.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm afraid to ask what those ways are.

jokes.text: Huh? Be best friends with you? Go out with you? Have a baby with you? Oh, wait a minute. I did all those things!
jokes.setup: Ross confronts Rachel, demanding to know what he has to do to get a goodbye.
jokes.punchline: He lists the extreme qualifications (best friends, dating, baby) — and then realizes he actually did ALL of them.
jokes.explanation: Strong escalation joke that also functions as a series-recap moment. The list structure builds perfectly — 'best friends,' 'go out with you,' 'have a baby' — and his genuine surprise at the realization ('Oh, wait a minute!') lands because the audience is ahead of him. Good character integration — this absurdist self-confrontation is very Ross. High structure score.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So what kind of gig do you have tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, I'm going to this corporate event. It's a bondage thing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: A bondage thing? Like... you're performing at a bondage thing?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, Mike thinks I am.

jokes.text: It is difficult to say goodbye to five people. Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye, goodbye, g-- / It's physically impossible!
jokes.setup: Ross sarcastically defends Rachel's inability to say goodbye to six people.
jokes.punchline: He attempts to say 'goodbye' six times and trails off before finishing — proving his sarcastic point accidentally.
jokes.explanation: Good bit of physical/verbal comedy — Ross's sarcastic demonstration accidentally proves his own point. 'It's physically impossible!' as the button works well and would be very funny in performance.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Rachel, I just want you to know that you mean so much to me, and I'm going to miss you so much when you—

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Pppppbbbbbttttt

jokes.text: I thought I was going home to bed, but I'm sensing there's something less fun for me to do here.
jokes.setup: Monica announces more packing needs to be done and Phoebe tries to leave.
jokes.punchline: Phoebe reads the room and resignedly acknowledges she's about to be conscripted into Monica's moving operation.
jokes.explanation: Decent Phoebe line — her passive-resignation is good character work. Functional but not standout.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I haven't cried like this in years!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You cried yesterday at a news story.

jokes.text: You couldn't be cool.
jokes.setup: Ross is separated from Phoebe to help in a different room by Monica, while Phoebe has to stay with Monica for packing.
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's flat, bitter 'You couldn't be cool' to Ross as he escapes Monica's regime.
jokes.explanation: Four-word button — maximum economy. Phoebe's resentment at being stuck with Monica while Ross escapes is relatable and funny, if not especially original.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Joey seems really calm about the whole thing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: *emotional breakdown*

jokes.text: If I'm harsh with you, it is only because you're doing it wrong.
jokes.setup: Monica gives Phoebe instructions for packing and warns her she'll be harsh.
jokes.punchline: Monica's explanation for her harshness — that the other person will inevitably be doing it wrong — is stated as fact.
jokes.explanation: Good Monica character joke — her certainty that harshness is JUSTIFIED because others will be wrong is a perfect encapsulation of her controlling nature. High character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh, I'm so lucky. Rachel didn't even say goodbye to me.

jokes.text: Who's that dirty old lady? / Monica's grandmother. / Oh, my God. Nana liked it rough!
jokes.setup: Joey finds photos in the closet that apparently show the handcuffs being used — by an elderly woman.
jokes.punchline: The photos reveal the handcuffs belonged to Monica's grandmother — 'Nana liked it rough!'
jokes.explanation: Excellent payoff to the entire handcuffs running gag. The reveal that it was Monica's grandmother all along — a deceased elderly woman — is a perfect dark comedy escalation. 'Nana liked it rough!' as the button is both shocking and very quotable. The structure of the running gag pays off here with maximum impact. The visual of the photos (inferred) adds to the cringe.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, technically, Rachel's goodbye was implicit, not explicit.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Which means it was understood without being directly stated—kind of like how I've been implicitly in love with her for years.

jokes.text: I keep getting these stomachaches. They come and go every few minutes.
jokes.setup: Erica describes what she thinks is a stomachache from eating too much at dinner.
jokes.punchline: The audience (and Monica) immediately recognize these as contractions — Erica doesn't realize she's in labor.
jokes.explanation: Classic dramatic irony setup — audience knows before character. The 'every few minutes' detail is the tell. Functional rather than exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I do not have too much pride! I can confront Rachel right now if I want to.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel! RACHEL! We need to talk about us!

jokes.text: Oh, my God. / Relax, we'll just get her some antacids.
jokes.setup: Monica realizes Erica is in labor; Ross is oblivious.
jokes.punchline: Ross's clueless suggestion of antacids for someone who is very obviously in labor.
jokes.explanation: Decent cluelessness gag but fairly predictable — the 'oblivious person suggests wrong remedy' joke is well-worn territory.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You didn't say goodbye? We had a thing, Rachel! We had a THING!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I was there when you got your first job. I was there when you got your first apartment. I was there when you got your first... everything!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: And you couldn't say goodbye?!

jokes.text: Oh, my God, we're gonna have a baby. We're gonna have a baby! Oh, my God, we're gonna have a baby! Oh, God, I've gotta sit down! I've gotta sit down!
jokes.setup: Monica announces Erica is in labor; everyone rushes into action.
jokes.punchline: Chandler's panic escalates through three identical exclamations of 'We're gonna have a baby!' before collapsing into needing to sit down — the exact opposite of action.
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler panic spiral — his inability to function under pressure is a core character trait. The escalation from excitement to collapse is good structure, though the execution is fairly broad.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'm not upset about not getting a goodbye. I'm upset that nobody seemed to care that I didn't get one.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Fine, fine. You want to see how easy it is to say goodbye? Watch this. Goodbye. Goodbye. Goodbye. Goodbye. Goodbye.

jokes.text: If you get a second, find out where she got that cheeseburger.
jokes.setup: Everyone is rushing Erica to the hospital in a labor emergency.
jokes.punchline: Joey's only concern as they leave is finding out the restaurant that served the amazing cheeseburger.
jokes.explanation: Perfect Joey joke — in the middle of an emergency, his food obsession takes complete precedence. 'If you get a second' acknowledges the emergency while still pursuing the food info, which makes it funnier than pure obliviousness. High character integration (this is the most Joey possible response to any situation) and very quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Where do you think you're going?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: To work.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, you're not.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm not?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No. You're going to help me clean this apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh, I see. So I'm not going to work, I'm going to... work.

jokes.text: Chandler, wait, wait, wait! / What? / If you get a second, find out where she got that cheeseburger.
jokes.setup: Monica, Chandler, and Erica are rushing to the hospital for the birth. Joey calls Chandler back urgently.
jokes.punchline: Joey's urgent request is to find out where Erica got the cheeseburger she mentioned earlier — in the midst of a baby being born, Joey's priority is restaurant sourcing.
jokes.explanation: A perfectly constructed Joey joke. The 'Chandler, wait!' creates urgency and misdirects toward something important; the pivot to restaurant research during a birth is a textbook Joey priority-inversion. The fact that he remembered the cheeseburger through all the chaos shows where his mind really lives. Character integration is near-perfect — this is the quintessential Joey joke. Well above the threshold for strong scoring.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could I BE any more organized? Oh wait, that's not me, that's Monica. She's like a human forklift.

jokes.text: Now give me your best shot. / All right, here goes. [pause] Doesn't work.
jokes.setup: Phoebe and Monica are doing something with bubble wrap in the closing scene — Monica appears to be wearing bubble wrap while Phoebe punches it.
jokes.punchline: After a dramatic build-up, Phoebe punches and... it doesn't pop. Anticlimactic deflation.
jokes.explanation: Callback to Chandler's earlier speculation that Phoebe was punching bubble wrap. The deadpan 'Doesn't work' as the final joke of the episode is a good low-key button — anticlimactic by design. The visual of them earnestly testing this is funnier on screen than on paper.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I know I'm being controlling, but it's only because I care. And also because your packing skills are a disaster and I can't watch you roll a sweater like some kind of animal.

tmdb_overview: Extremely pregnant Erica visits Monica and Chandler just as they are preparing to move to their new house in the suburbs. At the same time Rachel has packed and ready for her move to Paris, so on her last night in New York the gang hosts a farewell party for her. She says goodbye to each of her friends individually, except for Ross and he's offended. However, before the night is over, there will be more surprises.
insight: Bittersweet finale trades laugh density for emotional weight, landing 73 points.
